items.title: Chuck Findley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 6, 2023
items.q: he told Sal Nestico he says, “I want you to hear this kid.”

ctx.x: Oh absolutely. But once again I’m getting back to, it was fun you know, it was fun you know? Music should be fun. It should not be — well that’s why I chose not to be a classical player. I didn’t want to sit there and count a hundred bars and then come in. I wanted to play my horn. And that’s why every night I’d go — every night on the road I’d go to a club and play, with different players. That’s how I learned. That was the school — that was my college training, and learning how to play from different players…

wanted to see Bobby. And we were doing an R&B band, it was a wonderful R&B band and we were opening for him and we were rehearsing. And it was after they did their sound check and they took their break and we were rehearsing and he told Sal Nestico he says, “I want you to hear this kid.” So they didn’t leave, they went up and they sat all the way up in the very top of the venue to listen to me play. And Shew, Bobby and I, we’re like brothers, real brothers. And next thing you know I get a call to fly to New York…

That’s a fascinating backstory to all that. I want to take you back to your busy studio life. I came across one of those on-line Chuck Findley discographies, you know, the never- ending scroll. And I started to count, literally, and I said this is not going to work. But what I did see is that in 1979, according to this list, you played on 26 LPs. Like that’s more than two a month and everybody from Dolly Parton to Tom Scott. So I don’t have a question, it’s simply an observation. But I wonder if you can describe,…
